A distraction occurs when something, inside or outside the vehicle, causes the driver’s attention to be diverted away from driving. Even when this occurs for a very short period of time, the driver receives less relevant information than necessary to drive safely.

questions.help:
12 Distances
 
12.5 Safety distance
The safety distance is the minimum space that a driver should leave between their vehicle and the vehicle ahead of them. This should be sufficient and enable them to stop, without impacting and colliding with the vehicle ahead of them, in the case of hard or unexpected braking by the preceding vehicle (the vehicle ahead of them). For safety it should always be greater than the stopping distance of the vehicle.
Not respecting the safety distance from the vehicle in front of you is the main cause of rear-end crashes.
This distance should be increased when travelling at higher speeds or in reduced visibility, or where the road has low adhesion qualities and when the driver is unsure of the locality or lacks experience.
Not maintaining the safety distance with the vehicle driving ahead of you can cost 4 points.
 
(Página 180 del manual 'Learning to drive')

12 Distances
 
12.5 Safety distance
Any driver of a vehicle driving behind another must leave space that allows them to stop without colliding in the event of sudden braking, taking into account, in particular, speed, grip and braking conditions. However, a group of cyclists does not need to keep this distance, paying close attention to avoid collisions.
When it is possible for vehicles behind you to overtake, then in addition to leaving a sufficient separation distance so that in case of sudden braking by the vehicle ahead of you – you don’t crash into the back of it, you should additionally leave a gap to allow overtaking vehicles to overtake safely. (Note: that his rule is not applicable to a group of cyclists travelling together.)
Vehicles with a MAM greater than 3500 kgs, vehicles and combinations / sets of vehicles over 10m long, must keep a minimum safety distance of 50 m.

questions.help:
Road traffic collisions  
   
1 A public health problem
Moreover, in addition to the human drama, it is important to highlight the enormous economic impact (either directly or indirectly) that occurs as a result of a traffic collision.
Costs derived from road traffic accidents are classified as human, material, healthcare and administrative.
Human costs include the loss of lives, productive capacity and physical and psychological suffering. Material costs consist of damages caused on vehicles and their loads as well as on the road and the environment. Healthcare costs comprise first aid, care and treatment of the wounded, rehabilitation and adaptations. Administrative costs hold those of police officers and firefighters and insurance and services management.
People believe that an accident has little effect on them but the cost is borne by taxpayers. The cost of vehicle insurance is also affected, as premiums are affected by collision data and the cost of accidents.
For these reasons, various international organisations, including the World Health Organisation (WHO), believe that road collisions are a priority public health problem throughout the world.
There is a serious need to work together to reduce the high numbers of dead and seriously injured on the roads.

4.5 Changing a wheel
Some vehicles have, instead of a complete spare wheel, a wheel for temporary use (colloquially called a ‘space saving wheel’). This allows the vehicle to be driven to the nearest garage, where the wheel can be repaired or replaced.
Normally the maximum speed that the vehicle can be driven at with this temporary wheel fitted, is indicated on the wheel itself. However, as a general rule it is recommended that the vehicle is not driven more than 200 km and at a speed not exceeding 80 km/h.
(Página 73 del manual 'Learning to drive')

Journeys and defensive and efficient driving           
         
1 Preparation for the trip      
1.3 Accessories, spare parts and tools      
Cars
- The V-16 light-emitting hazard warning device.
- A certified, high-visibility reflective vest inside the interior of the vehicle. It must be visible from at least 150 metres away. If the vehicle is an escort vehicle, protecting and accompanying others, vests must be worn by the driver and each member of the crew.
- A full-size spare or a temporary tyre, with the tools needed to change tyres, or an alternative system to changing them that offers sufficient guarantees for the mobility of the vehicle. In these cases, the vehicles will be driven in observance of the limitations of each alternative.
(Página 270 del manual 'Learning to drive')

7 Obligations after a collision
7.1 Failure to provide assistance
Rendering help is obligatory; failing to give assistance is punishable by law for those who don’t:
Help the victims, when it is possible to do so without any risk to themselves.
Request help for the victims, when they are unable to assist them or there is a need to do so.
Stop having been involved in a collision, where there are casualties and flee the scene.

questions.help:
7 Seat belts  
   
7.1 Purpose and effectiveness
In addition, the seat belt keeps the person inside the protective cell.
(Many people are killed each year when they are catapulted from their vehicle having not worn a seat belt). The seat belt is useful for all kinds of collisions however, not just front impacts.
With the use of seat belt, deaths caused by road traffic collisions have dropped significantly. It is estimated that by being properly secured in a vehicle there is a reduction, of nearly a half, of the likelihood of being killed in a road traffic collision.
To be effective, the seat belt should be approved. In addition, it must be well anchored. The anchorage points and the fastening device (buckle) should be checked regularly and repairs should be undertaken if necessary.
The condition of the belt fabric should also be inspected, to ensure that it is not worn, cut or has frayed edges.
(Página 76 del manual 'Learning to drive')

5 Generic speed    
 
5.3 Minimum generic speed
It is not permissible to travel at an abnormally slow speed and slow down the normal circulation of other vehicles without a justified cause.
Therefore, it is prohibited to travel at a speed below the minimum limit, even if there are no other vehicles travelling on the roadway.
(Página 174 del manual 'Learning to drive')
